questions.question: What two design features distinguish the Foster method's sampling and assay strategy for AFB?

options.A: Hive-entrance eDNA swabbing paired with a dual-target qPCR for P. larvae
options.B: Whole-hive dismantling paired with single-target culture of P. larvae
options.C: Passive baseboard traps paired with 16S-only endpoint PCR
options.D: Brood-frame dissection paired with microscopy and an internal-control-free assay

questions.rationale: The method combines minimally disruptive entrance swabs with a multiplex assay targeting two P. larvae markers.
questions.evidence_quote: The Foster method is a novel environmental DNA sampling method using colony entrance swabs together with a dual-target qPCR for Paenibacillus larvae

questions.question: Why did the authors use the single-copy ftsZ marker rather than 16S to quantify spore levels?

options.A: 16S copy number varied among isolates, whereas ftsZ is single-copy and supports quantification
options.B: ftsZ amplified 3–5 cycles earlier than 16S and was more sensitive
options.C: 16S was absent from the clinical isolates, while ftsZ was present only in spores
options.D: The 16S target was too specific, while ftsZ detected all bacterial species

questions.rationale: Although 16S was analytically more sensitive, variable copy number made it unsuitable as a quantitative marker, so the single-copy ftsZ gene was used.
questions.evidence_quote: Therefore the use of the single copy ftsZ gene was used for quantification purposes using a standard curve

questions.question: How did the two AFBduo targets perform analytically on synthetic DNA standards?

options.A: Both reliably detected 4 copies per 10 µL reaction, with ftsZ and 16S efficiencies of 94% and 96%
options.B: Only ftsZ detected 4 copies per reaction, with 16S efficiency below 50%
options.C: Both detected 40 copies per reaction, with efficiencies of 99% and 80%
options.D: 16S detected 4 copies per reaction, while ftsZ detected 10,000 copies only

questions.rationale: The assay reached four-copy sensitivity for both targets and reported high multiplex efficiencies for ftsZ and 16S.
questions.evidence_quote: both target reactions in the assay able to reliably detect down to 4 copies per 10 µL reaction. The reaction targets amplified with high efficiency in the multiplex (ftsZ = 94% and efficiency for 16S = 96% )

questions.question: What relationship between 16S and ftsZ Cq values was expected and observed in positive material?

options.A: 16S typically amplified 3–5 cycles earlier because it is multicopy per bacterium
options.B: ftsZ typically amplified 3–5 cycles earlier because it is multicopy per bacterium
options.C: Both targets had identical Cq because each occurs once per genome
options.D: 16S amplified later because its sequence was less conserved among isolates

questions.rationale: The 16S target's multicopy nature produced lower Cq values, typically by three to five cycles.
questions.evidence_quote: the 16S target typically amplified 3-5 cycles earlier (i.e. lower Cq's) than the ftsZ target as expected, due to the multiple copies of the 16S sequence per AFB bacterium compared to the single copy ftsZ gene.

questions.question: How was a positive pooled entrance-swab sample followed up to identify the affected hive?

options.A: Pools of up to 12 swab eluates were screened, then remnant samples from positive pools were tested individually
options.B: All swabs were retested by culture, then the whole apiary was dismantled
options.C: A positive pool was assigned to its highest-Cq sample without individual testing
options.D: Pools were sequenced, and the hive with the dominant 16S allele was selected

questions.rationale: The pooling workflow preserved remnant material and tested individual contributors after a pool was positive for both markers.
questions.evidence_quote: The remnant samples from pools that tested positive for both markers, were then tested individually as described.

questions.question: What spore quantity corresponded to a 95% probability of clinical signs in the fitted analysis?
questions.rationale: The logistic-regression analysis linked at least 565,000 spores with a 95% probability of clinical signs.
questions.evidence_quote: a spore quantity of 565,000 or more, revealed a 95% probability of clinical signs being present in the hive.

questions.question: What practical advantage did entrance sampling offer over sampling bees or the entire baseboard?

options.A: It avoided dismantling and disrupting the hive while detecting clinically relevant infection levels
options.B: It produced higher spore counts than nurse bees in every sampled colony
options.C: It eliminated the need for DNA extraction by allowing direct qPCR on swabs
options.D: It detected only presymptomatic infection, unlike whole-baseboard sampling

questions.rationale: The discussion highlights nondisruptive access and similar swab levels from entrance versus whole-baseboard collection.
questions.evidence_quote: The ability to sample the hive through the entrance removed the need to dismantle and disrupt the hive as with the first two sample types (bees and whole baseboard swabbing).

questions.question: Which specific preclinical example demonstrated the potential of quantitative entrance-swab testing?

options.A: Hive 11 had no visible signs at sampling but showed clinical AFB at the beekeeper's inspection about two weeks later
options.B: Hive 12 had visible clinical signs at sampling but no P. larvae detected in its bees
options.C: Hive 11 had low spore levels in bees but high levels on new hiveware
options.D: Two hives were declared clinically infected solely because their 16S Cq values were late

questions.rationale: Hive 11 had levels resembling clinical cases before visible signs appeared at the next inspection roughly two weeks later.
questions.evidence_quote: at the next inspection by the beekeeper (approximately two weeks after sampling), hive 11 showed clinical signs of AFB and was destroyed

questions.question: What limitation did the authors note when bees carried high P. larvae levels but hiveware swabs were low or negative?

options.A: Recently established colonies on new hiveware may not yet have deposited spores at the entrance
options.B: Entrance swabs cannot detect spores from newly established colonies under any conditions
options.C: High bee levels indicate the ftsZ marker has failed in the hiveware samples
options.D: Low hiveware levels prove that clinical infection is absent from the colony

questions.rationale: The two discordant hives had new hiveware and were newly established from infected parent colonies, leaving insufficient time for spores to accumulate on the entrance surfaces.
questions.evidence_quote: there had not been enough time for spores to be deposited around the hive entrance surfaces.

questions.question: Which broader surveillance application did the authors propose for the entrance-swab DNA sample?

options.A: Testing for other bee pathogens or incursion pests using an appropriate qPCR assay
options.B: Replacing all apiary inspections with a universal 16S assay for any hive disease
options.C: Identifying bee genotypes by sequencing the swab's fungal DNA
options.D: Detecting only European foulbrood in countries where it is endemic

questions.rationale: The authors suggest the same sample could support other pathogen assays and biosecurity surveillance, contingent on appropriate qPCR targets.
questions.evidence_quote: the same DNA sample can be used to test for other bee pathogens.
